name: Jellyfin Federation
description: Aggregate content from multiple Jellyfin servers into unified virtual libraries
overview: The Jellyfin Federation Plugin allows you to create a unified media library by aggregating content from multiple remote Jellyfin servers. Stream content from any server without file synchronization.
changelog:
Fixed the real cause of "federated playback takes minutes to start, then stutters every ~20 seconds": Proxy-mode streaming already commits a Content-Length header covering the whole remaining file, and video players constantly open and cancel range requests as completely normal behavior (seeking, prefetching, probing). The server was treating each of those ordinary cancellations as a successful response and just returning - which left the underlying ASP.NET server to discover far fewer bytes were actually written than promised and forcibly reset the TCP connection instead of closing it cleanly. Players see a reset very differently from an ordinary closed connection: it looked like a hard streaming error on nearly every single range request, forcing expensive recovery (re-fetching playback info, rebuilding the media source) instead of just opening the next request. The connection is now aborted deliberately instead, so an ordinary cancelled request no longer looks like a crash.

Three more bugs found and fixed alongside it: a stream retry from a resumed offset now requires the remote to actually answer with a matching partial-content response, instead of accepting a plain 200-from-the-start answer and splicing it onto bytes already sent to the client (this was corrupting playback rather than just stalling it, for any remote/proxy that dropped the Range header on a retried request); an auto-resolved playback user was getting silently written into the saved server configuration and persisted to disk by any unrelated save, instead of staying in memory for the session; and an episode whose series wasn't synced yet was being created as a loose, disconnected item at the library root instead of being skipped and retried on a later sync.

164 tests (up from 161), including regression coverage that reproduces each of these against the pre-fix code.
